abstract:
<jats:p>
                    In this paper we construct indefinite theta series for lattices of arbitrary signature
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0010437X19007504_inline1"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$(p,q)$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    as ‘incomplete’ theta integrals, that is, by integrating the theta forms constructed by the second author with J. Millson over certain singular
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0010437X19007504_inline2"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$q$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    -chains in the associated symmetric space
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0010437X19007504_inline3"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$D$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    . These chains typically do not descend to homology classes in arithmetic quotients of
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0010437X19007504_inline4"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$D$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    , and consequently the theta integrals do not give rise to holomorphic modular forms, but rather to the non-holomorphic completions of certain mock modular forms. In this way we provide a general geometric framework for the indefinite theta series constructed by Zwegers and more recently by Alexandrov, Banerjee, Manschot, and Pioline, Nazaroglu, and Raum. In particular, the coefficients of the mock modular forms are identified with intersection numbers.
                  </jats:p>
title: On some incomplete theta integrals

reference.unstructured: [Zwe02] S. P. Zwegers , Mock theta functions, PhD thesis, University of Utrecht (2002), https://dspace.library.uu.nl/handle/1874/878.

reference.volume-title: Arithmetic geometry and automorphic forms, Volume in honor of the 60th birthday of Stephen S. Kudla
reference.author: Funke

reference.unstructured: [Kud13] S. Kudla , A note on Zwegers’ theta functions, Preprint (2013).
[Liv16] I. Livinskyi , On the integrals of the Kudla–Millson theta series, PhD thesis, University of Toronto (2016).
